title: The morning after
steps: Dawn breaks in the dormitory, and you hardly slept. Through the crack last night, the three of you heard that someone is going to do something to the brooms before today's flying lesson. You cannot tell anyone without owning that you were out of bed.
Let us go to the shed before breakfast. If we get there first, we can fix it ourselves and we need not tell anyone.
{Let us hurry and go right now!|What if it is locked, or worse, dangerous?}

The three of you walk down the gravel path behind the castle to the broom shed. The door is wide open. Inside, the peg rack is empty and the brooms lie on the floor: some in a neat row by the bench, and others half hidden in the straw.
Look, hidden in these twigs! It is a black knotted thread, an enchanted knot. With this, the broom would buck in the air and throw its rider. The voice said to do it to all of them.
But how many are there? You can hardly see them in the straw. There is a way to know how many things of a kind there are without seeing them all. I will show you.
